explanations.answer: They are opposites that don't mix
explanations.explanation: You've got it, baker. Righteousness and wickedness, light and darkness: Paul sets them side by side and asks what partnership or fellowship they could possibly have. The questions answer themselves, because nothing. That's the point he's making when he says not to be unequally yoked with unbelievers.

explanations.answer: They work best as a team
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. Paul asks what partnership righteousness can have with wickedness, and what fellowship light has with darkness. He's asking because the answer is none. These pairs don't team up, and that's his whole point.

explanations.answer: They are two names for one thing
explanations.explanation: Close, but no, friend. Paul isn't saying these pairs are the same. He asks, "For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?" Each pair is two different things, and he's asking what they could share.
That's it, baker! Paul says, "For we are the temple of the living God." Not a building, but the people. Makes me stand up a little straighter on my gold base.

I get why you'd pick it, friend, since a temple sounds like a building. But Paul says, "For we are the temple of the living God." He's talking about believers, the people themselves. He's asking what agreement the temple of God can have with idols, and then he tells them who that temple is.

Good guess, friend, but that's not what Paul says here. He says, "For we are the temple of the living God." The temple he's talking about is believers. So he's pointing at the people, and at the very folks reading his letter.

True, baker! God says, "I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people." Dwell with them AND walk among them. That's a God who promises to live right there with His people.

Ooh, I'd flip that one back, friend! It's true. Paul quotes God saying, "I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people." Dwell with them, walk among them: that's two promises in one breath. Nobody here is being told to wave at God from across the street, and I think that's the best news in the verse.

explanations.answer: Come out from among them and be separate
explanations.explanation: Right on, baker. The Lord says, "Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord." That "Therefore" ties it to everything before it, to the temple and to God dwelling with His people. It's a call to come out and be separate.

explanations.answer: Stay among them and be their light
explanations.explanation: It sounds nice, friend, but it's not what the line says. The Lord says, "Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord." The call is to come out and be separate, not to stay put.

explanations.answer: Go up to My temple and be cleansed
explanations.explanation: Nice try, friend, but a temple trip isn't in this line. The Lord says, "Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord." Paul did just say "…we are the temple of the living God." so I see how the temple stuck in your head. But the call here is to come out and be separate.
Oh, friend, this one goes the other way. The Lord says, "Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you." He doesn't say He'll turn them away. He says He will receive them.

False is right, baker! The Lord says, "Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you." Turned away? Go look for it, because it's not in that line. The only door in that sentence is the one swinging open to receive them. I've been shut in a drawer, so believe me, I notice an open door.

Yes, baker! The Lord says, "I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty." A Father, with sons and daughters in the very same line. I know a thing or two about being called Papa, and it's the best name I've got.
Good thinking, friend, but that's not the word here. The Lord Almighty says, "I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters…" He says Father. Hang onto that one, because it's warm.

I can see why you'd guess it, friend, but the Lord doesn't say it here. He says, "I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty." The word is Father, and it comes with sons and daughters.

That's the word, baker! Paul says, "…let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God." Holiness is what gets perfected. It's a whole-kitchen kind of cleaning, and it starts with the promises Paul just listed.
Patience is a good one, friend, and my oven could teach a class on it. But it's not the word Paul uses here. He says, "…perfecting holiness in the fear of God." Holiness is what he's talking about.

Knowledge is a fine thing, friend, but it isn't the word Paul picks. He writes, "…let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God." The blank is holiness. I know plenty of facts about cookies, and not one of them has ever cleaned my counter.
